Run three auto print head alignments.
Make sure High Speed is not selected.
Lower the dpi setting you selected to print.  If you selected 2880 dpi, lower                     the setting to 1440 dpi.

Make sure you use the correct profile settings.

faqs.question: When I turn on my product, I see the message 150c on the LCD. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Turn off the printer, then turn it back on.
When the print head begins to move, unplug the power cord from the power outlet.
Move the print head left, then right, then left, stopping on the left side of the printer.
Plug the printer back into the power outlet.
Turn the printer on.

faqs.question: I see the message Communication Error when I use a USB connection. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Delete all print jobs in the print queue.
Turn the printer off.
Note:
Make sure the USB cable is connected correctly.
Restart your computer. When the desktop appears, turn your printer on and follow the on-screen instructions.
Note:
If the problem continues, turn the printer off again and delete the printer in the list of printers. Then disconnect the USB cable from the printer and connect it again.

faqs.question: Can I disable the automatic ink change setting in the driver when I change my media from Photo to Matte or vice versa?
faqs.answer: No.

faqs.question: Does my product use ink from all the cartridges during the black ink change operation?
faqs.answer: No. The printer's ink valve design enables it to use only black ink during the ink change operation.

faqs.question: How long does the ink change operation take?
faqs.answer: It takes approximately 2½ minutes to switch from Photo Black to Matte Black, and about 3 minutes 30 seconds to switch from Matte Black to Photo Black.

faqs.question: Why is an ink change from Photo Black to Matte Black shorter and why does it use less ink?
faqs.answer: Because Matte Black ink can easily cover a small amount of Photo Black ink, the printer does not need to spend as much time cleaning the Photo Black ink from the print head as it does when cleaning the Matte Black ink.

faqs.question: Do I need a Black Ink Conversion Kit to change a Photo Black ink cartridge to a Matte Black ink cartridge (or vice versa)?
faqs.answer:
No. The Photo Black ink cartridge and the Matte Black ink cartridge are installed at the same time. The printer automatically switches to the correct type of ink when you change the
Media Type
in the driver.

faqs.question: Can my product use the Photo Black and Matte Black ink cartridges at the same time?
faqs.answer: No. When a print job requires the other black ink cartridge, the printer switches automatically. This process takes a few minutes and uses some ink.

faqs.question: What is the minimum ink droplet size?
faqs.answer: The minimum ink droplet size is 3.5 picoliters.

faqs.question: Is each ink cartridge designed to fit only in the correct slot for its color?
faqs.answer: Yes.

faqs.question: Do the ink cartridges use a CSIC chip to store ink parameters?
faqs.answer: Yes. The chip stores all the information about the cartridges.

faqs.question: Does the Matte Black ink cartridge come free inside my product box?
faqs.answer: Yes. A Matte Black ink cartridge is included with the printer.

faqs.question: How does Epson UltraChrome K3 ink technology reduce metamerism?
faqs.answer: The use of new pigments, resin encapsulation, three levels of black, and a new screening algorithm reduces the effects of metamerism and bronzing from both color and black-and-white prints to a level below what the human eye can detect.

faqs.question: How can I tell which black ink my product is currently using?
faqs.answer: The ink level gauge on the control panel shows which black ink is selected: Matte Black or Photo Black.

faqs.question: Does my product automatically switch between the Matte Black and the Photo Black ink cartridge when I change the media selection in the driver to a matte or photo ink media type?
faqs.answer: Yes. The printer automatically switches to the correct black ink, according to the media type selected.

faqs.question: What size ink cartridges are included with my product?
faqs.answer:
The printer comes with 80 ml (2.7 oz) cartridges. There are no high capacity ink cartridges available for this printer.
Note:
We recommend that you use genuine Epson ink cartridges. The use of other products may affect your print quality and longevity and could result in printer damage. Yields vary considerably based on images printed, print settings, paper type, frequency of use and temperature. For print quality, a variable amount of ink remains in the cartridge after the “replace cartridge” indicator comes on. The printer ships with full cartridges and part of the ink from the first cartridges is used for priming the printer.

faqs.question: How do Epson UltraChrome K3 inks achieve such a wide color gamut?
faqs.answer: The inks have higher-density pigments and new, higher-gloss resin encapsulation.

faqs.question: How does Epson UltraChrome K3 ink technology achieve such a high black density?
faqs.answer: Higher-density pigments, along with a new higher-gloss resin, produce a level of black density that approaches most dye-based printers.

faqs.question: Do I need to drain the ink cartridges before transporting my product?
faqs.answer: No.

faqs.question: If my workflow never requires an ink change, will the black ink I don't use dry or clog the ink system?
faqs.answer: No. The printer monitors ink changes, and if an ink change is not done within 6 months, the printer performs an ink change automatically to keep the ink flowing properly.

ink cover open button on the control panel for 3 seconds to unlock the ink cover.

faqs.question: How does Epson UltraChrome K3 ink technology reduce gloss differential?
faqs.answer: Gloss differential is reduced because of the higher-gloss resin encapsulation technology and the three-level black system. UltraChrome K3 ink technology dramatically reduces the effects of gloss differential from both color and black-and-white prints on even the glossiest media, such as Epson Premium Glossy Photo Paper, without a gloss optimizer.

faqs.question: Why does an ink change from Matte Black to Photo Black take more time and use more ink?
faqs.answer: All Matte Black ink needs to be flushed from the ink damper and print head; otherwise, the black areas on gloss or semi-gloss media will not have a consistent and uniform appearance.

faqs.question: Which type of ink system does my product use?
faqs.answer: The printer uses a pressurized ink system. This ensures positive ink flow even when the printer is used at higher elevations or if the floor is not completely level.

faqs.question: How much ink is used during the ink change operation?
faqs.answer: The printer uses approximately 1.6 ml when switching to Matte Black and approximately 4.6 ml when switching to Photo Black.

faqs.question: Can I replace the maintenance cartridge?

faqs.question: What is the capacity of the maintenance tank?
faqs.answer: The maintenance tank holds 600ml/20.3 oz. of which 300 ml is usable.

faqs.question: If I do a heavy volume of borderless printing, how can the ink build-up be cleaned so it does not leave ink marks on the back and edge of my media?
faqs.answer: The printer keeps track of borderless printing and location.  When needed, it performs a borderless pad cleaning by firing Light Black and Light Magenta ink through the heavily used borderless pad location to flush away the excess ink build-up.

faqs.question: Why are Epson UltraChrome K3 prints so scratch-resistant? Are fine art papers equally scratch-resistant?
faqs.answer:
Epson UltraChrome K3 ink technology uses a different method for “binding” the particle of pigment and the glossy resin encapsulation. This chemical process, called Crosslinking Chemistry, produces prints that are significantly harder than the previous Epson UltraChrome ink technology, so they are very scratch resistant when printed on normal resin-coated or photographic-grade media types.
Fine art papers also benefit, but pose another problem. Although the ink is harder to scratch off, the surface of the print can get “scuffed” and the print will appear to have a “scratch” (similar to moving your hand across a suede jacket). The ink does not come off, but the print may still be damaged.

faqs.question: I am having trouble manually loading media into the rear manual feed slot. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Make sure that the product is turned on and READY appears on the LCD.
Attach the rear sheet guide to the back of the product.
Slide the left edge guide to the left so it is slightly wider than the width of                     your paper.
Insert one sheet face up and short edge first into the rear sheet guide against                     the right edge guide.
Slide the left edge guide against the left edge of the paper.
Gently guide the paper into the slot until it meets resistance.  Maintain a                     constant pressure; after a few seconds you'll feel the product pull the paper                     into printing position.
Use both hands to pull out and extend the output tray, lifting it slightly as                     you pull. Make sure the arrow marks on the tray and the printer are aligned.

faqs.question: What does the Common Updater 7.0 file do?
faqs.answer: The Common Updater 7.0 file provides the latest Mac OS X 10.6 support for your printer driver. Before installing the updater, make sure the most current version of the Mac OS X 10.5 or 10.6 printer driver is installed on your computer. Restart your computer after installing the updater.

faqs.question: Why are only matte media types displayed in the driver's media list?
faqs.answer: When the printer is using the Matte Black ink, only matte media types are displayed in the driver list. The complete media list appears only when the printer uses the Photo Black ink cartridge.

faqs.question: How do I update the firmware on my product's main board and the built-in network port?
faqs.answer:
Use the Epson LFP Remote Panel Utility to do the update. You can also use the
EpsonNet Config Utility
to update the network port firmware, but the network port must be connected to the printer through an ethernet connection (a USB connection will not work). To download the utilities, see the Download tab for the Stylus Pro 3800.

faqs.question: Why should I use the Matte Black mode?
faqs.answer: The standard Photo Black ink has been optimized for resin-coated and photographic-grade media types. If you're printing on matte-type papers such as Epson Velvet Fine Art, Enhanced Matte, or UltraSmooth Fine Art, the black density is significantly better with the Matte Black ink.

faqs.question: What are the minimum and maximum User-Defined paper sizes I can select?
faqs.answer: The minimum is 3.5 x 5 in (89 x 127 mm) and the maximum is 17 x 37.4 in (432 x 950 mm).

faqs.question: The Advanced B/W setting is grayed out in my product software. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Make sure you install the correct black ink cartridge for the media type selected. When the photo black cartridge is installed, the
Advanced B/W
setting is available only for glossy media types. It is not available for any of the matte media types. When the matte black cartridge is installed, the
Advanced B/W
setting is available only for matte media types.
If you're using the correct black ink cartridge for your media type but the
Advanced B/W
setting is still grayed out, then do the following:
Open the Hard Drive.
Select >
Applications
>
Utilities
>
Printer Setup Utility
.
Select your printer and click
Utility
.
Make sure you see the ink levels in the
Status Monitor
window, then click
Update
.
Restart the computer.

faqs.question: What is the Epson Advanced Black & White Printing Mode?
faqs.answer: This is a proprietary Epson screening and color management technology designed specifically to produce professional-level black and white prints. This unique screen technology takes advantage of our three-level black technology—along with Yellow, Light Cyan, and Light Magenta—to produce professional black and white prints from either color or grayscale files.

faqs.question: How do I know which Platen Gap setting is selected on my product?
faqs.answer:
If a non-standard (Widest, Wider, Wide, or Narrow) setting is selected, an indicator will appear on the printer's control panel. If you don't see an indicator, the setting is set to
STANDARD
(1.2 mm).

faqs.question: Where can I get the latest version of the Epson Communication Driver for my printer?
faqs.answer: Download the Communication Driver from the Downloads tab on your product's support page.

faqs.question: I can't find the Fine Art paper option in Windows. What should I do?

Manual - Rear
or
Manual - Front
) as your paper source in the printer driver. You see the Fine Art media choices. See your product's User's Guide to determine which black ink to use for your media type.

Adding a Printer in macOS 12 or Later

faqs.question: How do I add my Epson printer to the Printer list in macOS 12 or later?
faqs.answer:

faqs.question: Which interfaces does my product support?
faqs.answer: It includes one Hi Speed USB 2.0 (1.1 compatible) port and one 10/100Base-T Ethernet port.

faqs.question: Is there my product cover available for my product?
faqs.answer: Yes, there is an optional printer cover (C3800TUMI) available.

faqs.question: Is an extended warranty available for my product?
faqs.answer: Yes, there are two plans available. A One-Year extended warranty (part# EPP38B1, MSRP $179.00) and a Two-Year extended warranty (part# EPP38B2, MSRP $319.00).

faqs.question: How do I get service for my product I purchased in another country?
faqs.answer:
Please visit the appropriate Epson website by selecting the region where the printer was purchased from the
Epson Global website
. Due to differences in products sold in other countries, printers need to be serviced in the country of origin.

faqs.question: How many nozzles does the print head have?
faqs.answer: The print head consists of 8 nozzle columns (one for each color) and each column has 180 nozzles.  Matte Black and Photo Black share a nozzle column.

faqs.question: What is the size of my product with all the covers and paper trays extended?
faqs.answer: 684 mm x 579 mm x 962 mm (26.93 in x 22.8 in x 37.9 in)

faqs.question: Which covers must be open during printing?
faqs.answer: The front cover must be open when the printer is feeding paper from any of the three paper paths. If you're using the auto sheet feeder, it must also be open.

faqs.question: How does the High Speed setting in my product driver work?
faqs.answer: When High Speed is selected, the print head prints in both directions to speed up printing. When High Speed is turned off, the printer prints in one direction only, which produces the highest quality images.

faqs.question: How long is the warranty on my product?
faqs.answer: One year. The printer is covered by Epson's One-Year Preferred Protection Plan. You can also purchase a One-Year extended warranty (part# EPP38B1, MSRP $179.00) or a Two-Year extended warranty (part# EPP38B2, MSRP $319.00).

faqs.question: What is the maximum USB cable length I can use to connect my product?
faqs.answer: The maximum cable length supported is 10 feet (3 meters).

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.
